main_point: Michael Moore's upcoming documentary 'Sicko,' which criticizes the U.S. healthcare system by contrasting it with Cuba's model, has been leaked online and is under federal investigation for violating the Cuban embargo, while the film's release faces opposition from health insurance companies.

aliases: Office of Foreign Assets Control within the United States Department of the Treasury

statements.text: Lionsgate Studios, the distributor, has faced a second pre-release leak this month. The film 'Sicko' was shared on peer-to-peer networks. This movie criticizes the U.S. healthcare system by contrasting it with Cuba's model. These leaks hurt the planned release strategy. They also create worry about how the film will affect public discussion on healthcare reform before it officially opens.
statements.text_short: A leaked copy of the controversial healthcare documentary 'Sicko' marks a second pre-release breach for its distributor.

statements.text: The documentary 'Sicko' highlights a stark contrast between the U.S. and Cuba's healthcare systems by documenting how 9/11 volunteers denied aid in the United States were able to receive free treatment in Havana. This comparison, which includes data showing an inhaler costs five cents in Cuba versus 120 dollars in the U.S., serves as evidence that the current American system fails to provide affordable care even to those with insurance, thereby challenging the necessity of the existing private-sector-dominated model.
statements.text_short: The film 'Sicko' uses the case of 9/11 victims to argue that the U.S. healthcare system is fundamentally broken compared to Cuba's model.

statements.text: In response to the release of the documentary 'Sicko,' which calls for a healthcare system modeled after Canada, France, or the UK, the health insurance industry insists that the United States must develop a unique solution. This approach requires the public and private sectors to work together to ensure everyone has access to high-quality, affordable healthcare, rejecting the notion of adopting a foreign system in favor of a hybrid domestic reform.
statements.text_short: Health insurance companies oppose adopting foreign healthcare models, advocating instead for a unique American hybrid of public and private sectors.
